Indicator 1.1.1: National/Peacekeeping Mission-Level outcome indicator: # of peacekeeping operations’ political strategies/mission plans/mission concepts that include POC as a priority objective

Indicator 1.5.1: National and International-Level outcome indicator: # of steps taken at UN headquarters and by peacekeeping operations to track and address harm to civilians that could result from its own presence, activities, and operations and the operations of other armed actors that they support
Indicator 1: # of institutions strengthened (in terms of responsiveness to needs and rights of the population)

Indicator 1.5.2: International/UN Secretariat or Member State-Level outcome indicator: # of reports, statements, mandates, policies, votes, strategic reviews, etc. (that we sought to influence) produced by policy- and decision-makers at the international-level that acknowledge the importance of or call on UN peacekeeping operations to mitigate harm to civilians
Indicator CC7: # of requests for CIVIC advocacy products or information (including speaking invitations)

Indicator 1.2.2: International/UN Secretariat or Member State-Level outcome indicator: # of reports, statements, mandates, policies, votes, etc. (that we worked to influence) produced by policy- and decision-makers at the international-level supporting increased use of threats-based analysis, including gender-sensitive analysis, in peacekeeping operations’ planning and decision-making

Indicator 1.3.2: International/UN Secretariat or Member State-Level outcome indicator: # of reports, statements, mandates, policies, votes, strategic reviews, etc. (that we sought to influence) produced by policy- and decision-makers at the international-level that call for 1) mandates to be matched by adequate capabilities; 2) mandates and capabilities to match the mission context (e.g. threats against civilians); and 3) that mission drawdown and withdrawal is done along appropriate timelines based on benchmarks, conflict analysis/threat assessments of violence against civilians, and the ability to hand over mission tasks to other actors
Indicator CC5: # of attendees at CIVIC-organized events (including roundtables)
Indicator CC3: # of interviews conducted by CIVIC with peacekeeping stakeholders at the national- and international-level

Indicator 1.4.1: International/UN Secretariat or Member State-Level outcome indicator: # of steps taken by the UN Secretariat to improve special investigations, release findings and recommendations from investigations, and/or ensure remedial actions are taken for patterns of under-performance or egregious failures of peacekeeping operations to protect civilians
Indicator CC4: # of CIVIC-organized events (including roundtables) (sensitization/advocacy) that CIVIC held in our four countries of focus, New York, Washington, DC and key European capitals

Indicator 1.1.2: International/UN Secretariat or Member State-Level outcome indicator: # of UN Secretariat or Member State reports, statements, mandates, policies, votes, etc. that we worked to influence produced by policy- and decision-makers at the international-level supporting POC as a priority in peacekeeping

Indicator 1.6.1: National and International-Level outcome indicator: # of new/revised policies, guidance, or practices developed by the UN Secretariat or a peacekeeping mission to influence how peacekeeping operations undertake safe and effective engagement with communities under threat, including gender-sensitive community engagement

Indicator 1.2.1: National/Peacekeeping Mission-Level outcome indicator: # of steps taken in peacekeeping missions to improve how threat assessments, including gender-sensitive assessments, are linked to planning and decision-making

Indicator 1.4.2: International/UN Secretariat or Member State-Level outcome indicator: # of steps taken by Member States that call on the UN Secretary-General/Secretariat to share the findings and recommendations of investigations and to regularly update Member States and other stakeholders on actions taken to implement the recommendations

Indicator 1.3.1: National- and International-Level outcome indicator: # of instances that peacekeeping operations propose, the Fifth Committee approves, or peacekeeping operations reallocate resources for key personnel, tools, and assets to improve: how threat assessments are linked to planning and decision-making, civilian harm mitigation, community engagement, and other key protection functions
Indicator CC8: # of documented instances of civilian feedback used to design or modify CIVIC’s programs, policies, advocacy, tools, reports, and other products
Indicator CC2: # of private advocacy briefs and recommendations that we intend to produce per year to influence international- and national-level policies, practices, procedures, and decisions
Indicator CC1: # of reports/policy briefs/issue briefs/op-eds/blogs produced by CIVIC to influence international- and national-level policies, practices, procedures, and decisions
